meanings.note: informal: a group of young men; ребята! = guys!
Secondary conversational sense ('kids, children') (colloquial plural of ребёнок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The boys will have a word with you.

examples.text: Тогда ребята с тобой поработают. До свидания, Аркадий Борисович.
examples.trans: Then the boys will have a little word with you. Goodbye, Arkady Borisovich.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.en: to have to, to be forced to
meanings.note: impersonal with dative: мне придётся = I'll have to

examples.trans: I'm going to have to torture you.
We had to wait a long time.

examples.text: Ты что, очкарик, не понимаешь? Мне тебя мучить придётся.
examples.trans: Don't you get it, four-eyes? I'm going to have to torture you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'статься'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to break up', forming an aspectual pair with 'расставаться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.text: Нет, я всё решил! Мы с ней точно расстанемся.
examples.trans: No, I have decided everything! She and I will definitely break up.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'where'.

examples.trans: Wait, where are you two going?

собраться.gloss: to get ready, plan to, gather

meanings.en: to intend, plan, get ready to
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обраться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to get ready', forming an aspectual pair with 'собираться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.
Secondary conversational sense ('to gather, assemble') (reflexive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ты что, уходить от меня собрался?
examples.trans: Are you planning to leave me or what?
Are you planning to drink alcohol?

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('so') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('like that, so') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'early'.

examples.text: Муж тоже там работал. И рано умер.
examples.trans: My husband worked there too. And he died young.
Tomorrow I need to get up early.

examples.text: Что, по домам? Мне завтра рано вставать.
examples.trans: What, time to go home? I have to get up early tomorrow.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'волить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to fire', forming an aspectual pair with 'увольнять'.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'how'.
Secondary conversational sense ('as') (как вы знаете = as you know) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'too'.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

meanings.en: to leave, to go away (on foot)
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ходить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to leave', forming an aspectual pair with 'уйти'.

examples.text: Уходи отсюда скорее, пока шеф не увидел тебя без формы!
examples.trans: Get out of here quickly before the chef sees you without a uniform!

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Secondary conversational sense ('tell me / tell us') (polite request) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to do', forming an aspectual pair with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: О, это, Аркашенька, бывает очень часто.
examples.trans: Oh, that happens very often, Arkashenka.
We often meet in the park.
I used to come see you often.

meanings.en: to step, to stride, to march
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to step'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('! = off you go, get moving') (colloquial, brusque) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Вот когда выйдешь, тогда и дам. Шагай.
examples.trans: When you get out of here, then I'll give it to you. Off you go.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'пасть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to disappear, vanish'.

examples.text: Аркадий, что делать будем? Самсонов пропал.
examples.trans: Arkady, what are we going to do? Samsonov is missing.

examples.text: Таня, а куда пропал твой бывший муж?
examples.trans: Tanya, and where did your former husband disappear to?

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'because of' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('from behind') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амоуверенность'). Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'overconfidence, self-assurance, arrogance' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: That was your overconfidence flashing by.

examples.text: Это ваша самоуверенность промелькнула. Спокойной ночи!
examples.trans: That was your overconfidence flashing by. Good night!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лишком').

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'a lot'.
Secondary conversational sense ('more') (comparative) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('here') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('! = you'll see!') (emphasis) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'final pay', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Ну, именно на это был расчёт.
examples.trans: Well, that was the exact calculation.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
followed by genitive plural in nominative/accusative

examples.text: Я уже вам сто раз говорила. Я брала двадцать тысяч, вернула тридцать!
examples.trans: I've already told you a hundred times. I borrowed twenty thousand, paid back thirty!

meanings.note: the noun after it is genitive plural: тысячи мест

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'remaining' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.trans: And where are the rest of the children?
The rest of the books were lying on the table.

examples.text: Скоро арестуют и Осипенко, и остальных.
examples.trans: Soon they will arrest both Osipenko and the others.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: the 'е' drops out in the other forms
Secondary conversational sense ('' ' = over and out') (radio and phone phrase) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: At the end of the film everyone is happy.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'month', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: I've been living here for a month.
The election is in a month.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.
